inputs.rationale: This change adds no property and no API surface: the page states there is no new CSS property or JavaScript API, so there are no programmatic inputs to document; the trigger is user interaction, which the #the-behavior table enumerates instead.

outputs.rationale: The feature has no return value: its observable effect is a rendering change on an existing value (text-overflow: ellipsis), described in the #the-behavior table rather than returned to script.

errors.rationale: The page documents no error or exception path: the interaction is a rendering behaviour with no throwing surface, and no failure mode is listed in the #the-behavior table.

context.rationale: The page scopes this to a rendering change on an existing value in Chrome 147 (behind the experimental-flags enablement shown in #at-a-glance), with no separate context, worker, or global configuration to document.

lifecycle.rationale: There is nothing to construct or tear down in script: the page frames the change as purely in the rendering model, so no lifecycle or cleanup surface exists beyond the browser's own layout cycle.

securityPrivacy.rationale: This is a purely presentational CSS rendering behavior with no input, storage, or cross-origin access implications.
